title: Driving forces for change

changes: Add globalisation, innovation and cutting costs as examples of forces for change, since the new point lists them and the card does not.
Adjust the card's wording to the Victorian Business Management course, for example by using its 'macro environment' terminology alongside 'business environment'.
match.reason: The bank card teaches the same idea of internal and external forces pushing a business to change at a matching depth, but it needs a few example and terminology changes to match the new point's list and this Victorian course.

confirm.reason: The closest bank point (bus-forces-change) sorts forces into internal and external with a few examples, but the VCE point teaches the study design's own list of driving forces (owners, managers, employees, competitors, legislation, profit, cost cutting, globalisation, technology, innovation, societal attitudes), which needs different content and questions.

draft.title: Driving forces for change
card: A driving force is a pressure that pushes a business to change. Some come from inside the business and some from outside it.
owners who want a new direction, managers with new plans, employees who suggest better ways to work, and the aim of earning more profit or cutting costs.
competitors that win customers, new laws, globalisation (the growing links between countries), new technology and changing social attitudes, such as concern for the environment.
Innovation, which is turning a new idea into a new product or process, can also push a business to change. Any of these forces can lead to change, but none of them forces it to happen.
draft.remember: Driving forces are pressures from inside or outside a business that can push it to change.

a.q: Several customers of a Geelong bakery now ask for plant-based food, so the owner adds it to the menu. Which driving force is this?
a.why: Customers' changing views and tastes are a shift in social attitudes, which is an outside force. The owner is not responding to a law, a rival or staff, so those options are wrong.
a.clue: Who is asking for the change, and what has shifted?

b.q: Tariq runs a Ballarat firm that makes bike parts. A rival starts selling similar parts at lower prices, so Tariq buys new machines to cut his costs. Which is the best description of the driving force?
opts: A competitor, an outside force that pushed him to act
Technology, an inside force that he chose to adopt
Profit, an outside force that was set by his rival
Owners, an inside force that the rival created
b.why: The rival's lower prices are what pushed Tariq to act, and a competitor is an outside force. The new machines are how he responded, so technology is the change he made, not the pressure behind it.
b.clue: Ask what happened first to make him act, not what he bought.

b.best: A competitor, an outside force that pushed him to act
